title: Transparent fallback limiter and sensitivity-based load trimmer
author: Avery Chen
description:
Background and motivation: Recent incidents showed oscillations when regional capacity drops: aggressive fallback routing + blunt load-shedding caused tenant-visible latency spikes and some request drops. Operators requested a mechanism to (1) transparently cap fallback traffic to protect hotspots, (2) slowly trim non-critical traffic based on real-time sensitivity signals, and (3) emit clear telemetry so rollouts can be safely observed and tuned.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds a transparent fallback limiter that applies a soft cap to fallback routing; introduces a sensitivity-based load trimmer which scores requests by sensitivity (request type, tenant SLAs, presence of kv-cache hits, token budget) and trims lower-sensitivity requests preferentially; integrates metrics and tracing for visibility; provides a config-driven ramp for gradual rollout and an emergency bypass.

Design notes and rationale: The limiter sits in the routing layer and is intentionally conservative: it never hard-blocks eligible fallbacks, instead it returns a controlled "soft-drop" response token (HTTP 429 with Retry-After hint + structured reason) for trimmed requests. Sensitivity scoring is pluggable so experiment signals (e.g., prompt tags or route metadata) can be used without code changes. We prioritized 1) minimal critical-path latency impact (fast path checks only), 2) predictable unit-economics (rough token savings estimation per trim), and 3) observability (per-tenant/route counters and histograms).

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of limiter and trimmer in routing runtime - [x] Unit tests for trimming heuristics and limiter boundary conditions - [x] Integration smoke test simulating regional capacity degrade - [x] Metrics (prometheus) + tracing spans added - [x] Config knobs (percent cap, sensitivity thresholds, emergency-bypass) - [x] Docs: short console-runbook and feature flag gating

Commits (high-level): - Add transparent fallback limiter and pluggable sensitivity scorer - Wire scoring into router decision path and expose config - Add prometheus metrics and tracing spans + console runbook - Add unit tests for scorer, limiter boundary cases - Add integration smoke test with simulated regional egress constraint - Address review feedback: tighten metric labels, add guardrail for missing metadata

Changed areas (high level): - pkg/router/fallback_limiter.go (new) - pkg/router/sensitivity_scorer.go (new, pluggable interface) - services/routing/router.go (integration points, ~20 LOC) - telemetry/metrics/fallback_metrics.yaml (prometheus exporters) - scripts/integration-tests/fallback_smoke.test (new smoke test) - docs/runbooks/fallback-limiter.md (operational runbook) - config/defaults.yaml (feature flag + params) - pkg/router/limiter_test.go, pkg/router/scorer_test.go

Testing and CI: Initial run failed on a flaky integration test (timeout in fallback_smoke). Reproduced locally, increased test harness timeout and made the smoke test deterministic by seeding simulated latency. Subsequent CI run passed all checks (unit, linters, integration smoke). CI summary: unit-tests (pass), lint (pass), integration-tests (pass), e2e (not included in this PR), perf-regressions (no significant delta in benchmark CI).

Review conversation (condensed): Marcus Rivera: "Can you avoid allocating in the hot path for scoring? We should keep the fast path zero-allocation."
Avery Chen: "Good catch — changed scorer to return primitive score and use call-site caching; added micro-benchmark (pkg/router/bench) showing negligible overhead."

Priya Nair: "Metric labels may include high-cardinality tenant IDs; please ensure we only emit tenant id as a hashed label or use a separate high-card gateway metric."
Avery Chen: "Switched per-tenant metrics to use tenant_bucket label (coarse bucketing) and added a paid/free tier label; kept a sampled detailed counter behind feature flag for debugging."

Liam O'Connor: "Edge-case: requests without route metadata should default to highest sensitivity so we don't inadvertently trim unknowns."
Avery Chen: "Addressed; default score is high-sensitivity and documented in runbook."

Approvals: Marcus Rivera (approved), Priya Nair (approved), Liam O'Connor (approved).

Operational guidance and rollout plan: Gate the feature behind a config flag (defaults disabled). Initial rollout: 5% of fallback traffic in staging for 48h with metrics dashboard (fallback_rate, trimmed_rate by sensitivity_bucket, request_latency_p90). If stable, ramp to 25% -> 75% over two days. Emergency bypass available via feature flag and an on-path header that forces bypass for specific tenants.

Release notes: Adds a transparent fallback limiter and a sensitivity-based load trimmer to reduce tenant-visible impact during regional capacity stress. The feature is behind a flag; operators should follow the runbook to monitor trimmed rates and p90 latency.

Related work: ENG-1942 (regional fallback stabilization), ENG-1987 (telemetry for soft-shedding).

release_notes: Transparent fallback limiter + sensitivity-based trimming behind a feature flag. Improves graceful degradation during regional capacity stress with minimal latency overhead.
footprint_estimate: Estimated token savings: ~8-12% under high fallback load (internal benchmark).
